autoimporta.title: Autoimporta
autoimporta.subtitle: Financial-data automation and normalization platform
autoimporta.description: A platform that ingests financial documents from email, FTP and the web, converts and normalizes them against business rules, and delivers them to production systems — automatically, monitored and reliably.
autoimporta.fullDescription: A financial-services company received quotes, time series and KIID documents from dozens of heterogeneous sources (Excel/CSV/PDF/XML email attachments, FTP servers, web portals), in inconsistent formats handled manually. Autoimporta removes the manual work: it intercepts the files, recognizes sender and content, converts and normalizes them against business rules, and delivers them downstream with no human intervention. An ongoing consulting engagement, including the migration of the codebase to PHP 8.3 / Laravel 12. The system spans 51 data models, around 71 Artisan commands and 19 queued asynchronous jobs.

challenges.title: Multi-channel ingestion
challenges.solution: Automatic acquisition from email (IMAP), FTP and automated web downloads with headless scraping, routed via pattern matching on sender, subject and body.

challenges.title: Conversion pipeline with failover
challenges.solution: A chain of 10 specialized Excel/CSV/PDF/XML converters: if one fails, another automatically takes over without losing the data.

challenges.title: Financial normalization
challenges.solution: A rules engine over ISIN codes, dates and values, with CRC-32 hash deduplication to avoid re-importing already processed files.

challenges.title: Monitoring and alerting
challenges.solution: 13 processes under continuous monitoring with heartbeats, health checks, stuck-process detection and multi-level alerts with Microsoft Teams notifications.

privacyFeatures: Code and infrastructure owned by the client
Database-driven dynamic scheduling: new sources and rules via configuration, not deployment
Client name and business details covered by an NDA

finance.title: Kiba.Finance
finance.subtitle: Personal finance with double-entry accounting
finance.description: A personal-finance tool built on double-entry accounting: transactions, assets, budgets and reports. Laravel 12 + Filament 4, local data, privacy-first.
finance.fullDescription: A complete rewrite in Laravel 12 and Filament 4 of a previous Django application for personal financial management. At its core is a double-entry accounting engine: every transaction must balance (debit = credit), with a hierarchical chart of accounts, asset management (stocks, real estate, crypto), monthly budgets and financial reports (balance sheet, income statement, cash flow, savings, portfolio). Designed privacy-first: data stays local, with no mandatory account or bank integration.

challenges.title: Double-entry accounting
challenges.solution: An engine that enforces debit/credit balancing and the correct normal balance for each account type at the model level.

challenges.title: Django-to-Laravel rewrite
challenges.solution: A full migration of the domain and data from the previous Python application to a modern PHP stack.

challenges.title: Dynamic financial reports
challenges.solution: Reports whose calculations respect each account's normal balance, with charts updated in real time via Livewire.

privacyFeatures: No account or bank access required

fetch.title: Kiba.Fetch
fetch.subtitle: Scraping and document intelligence for financial data
fetch.description: A multi-tenant platform to extract structured data from sites and financial documents (KIID/PRIIP). Three-service architecture: a Laravel/Filament control plane plus Python scraper and AI services. In development.
fetch.fullDescription: A platform — in active development — for automatically extracting structured data from websites and financial documents. The architecture separates three services communicating through PostgreSQL: a Laravel/Filament control plane for UI, scheduling and template management; a Python (asyncio) scraper with anti-detection failover; a Python/FastAPI AI service for OCR and PDF extraction. Designed multi-tenant from day one. The foundation and scraping job execution are operational; template auto-repair and billing are on the roadmap.

challenges.title: Decoupled service architecture
challenges.solution: Three independent services sharing only the PostgreSQL database, with a job queue handled via SKIP LOCKED polling.

challenges.title: Multi-tenancy from the start
challenges.solution: Tenant isolation at the application and database level, designed for SaaS from day one.

challenges.title: Resilient scraping
challenges.solution: A headless browser engine with automatic failover between engines when bot detection triggers.

privacyFeatures: Multi-tenant isolation at application and DB level
Ethical scraping, respecting rate limits and site rules

transparency.section_resources_intro: The browser loads static resources (fonts and icons) from public CDNs to reduce loading time. These resources don't install cookies but their provider can log the request IP:
transparency.section_resources_outro: We're working to self-host these resources too, removing every third-party request. When done, the change will be noted here.

transparency.section_verify_p1: Open your browser's developer tools (F12), "Network" tab, and reload the page. You'll see exactly all the requests made and you can compare them against what's stated above.
transparency.section_verify_p2_prefix: If you find a discrepancy, write to us at
transparency.section_verify_p2_suffix: and we'll fix it: either this page, or the site.
transparency.section_why_p: Selling "privacy first" as a slogan is easy. Making it verifiable is the point. This page exists because we believe technical transparency is the most honest way to demonstrate what we claim.
